newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 notches up three-day record run.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 notches up three-day record run.

text.p: UK shares staged a blistering rally on Wednesday with the lead index chalking up its third record close in as many days to come within grasping distance of the psychologically important 5,000 level.

"One is slightly at a loss for words," said Nick Knight, strategist at Nomura. "It would not appear to be fundamentally justified but this is a very powerful move and it would be extremely rash to deny it...one has to be careful about writing it off as madness."
The FTSE 100 ended 64.9 points or 1.3 percent higher at 4,964.2 after easing back from a new all-time high of 4,991.8.

UK blue-chips had faltered on the brink of the 5,000 hurdle as the Dow failed in its own attempt to hold above the key 8,000 level which it broke today for the first time. The U.S. index was up 25 points, just below the 8,000 mark as London closed.

Dealers said UK shares continued to benefit from incoming cash plus a shortage of stock but the dollar's recent ascent provided an extra boost. "The dollar's rise is supportive of all equity markets across Europe and you only have to look at what happened in France and Germany today to see that anything with dollar exposure is doing well," said Graham Smith, investment analyst at NatWest Stockbrokers.
"Tokyo and Hong Kong have also been doing well and it seems that all the major equity markets are acting in synch," he said.
Germany's DAX was up 1.94 percent whilst leading French shares climbed 1.2 percent, setting a fresh record high.
"There is an immense amount of liquidity globally," Smith added. "But the gains are limited to the blue-chips."
Banks, pharmaceuticals and oils were the leaders in London, with the bank sector contributing almost half of the FTSE's rise as institutions struggled to increase weightings.
"This rally has further to go...just look at the shortage of quality stock where the sectors are in fashion," a dealer said.
"Drugs, oils and banks are absolutely through the roof...there is a lot of money looking for a safe home."
Second-line stocks, were better on the day but much more subdued. The Mid-250 added 36 points to 4,487.5, its highest level for a month. The All-Share was up 26 points to 2,316.
Among individual share movers HSBC Holdings Plc ended 68p higher at 21.54 stg, Barclays Plc rose 30-1/2p to 12.82-1/2 stg and Standard Chartered Plc was up 37-1/2p to 10.42 stg.
The most active stock of the day was British Telecommunications Plc which bucked the market trend to finish 8-1/2p down at 437p on worries over the group's planned merger with MCI Communications.

Shares in Guinness Plc rose 14-1/2p to 620-1/2p and Grand Metropolitan Plc was up 16-1/2p to 622-1/2p after French luxury goods maker LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton announced a plan to merge its drinks business with Guinness and Grandmet.
The worst performance of the day came from compact disc and computer tape maker Plasmon Plc which issued a profits warning. The shares plunged 85-1/2p or 47 percent to 93-1/2p.
Zeneca PLC climbed 64-1/2p to 22.62-1/2 stg and oil stocks British Petroleum Plc and Shell Transport and Trading Plc were both 10-1/2p better at 807p and 434-1/2p respectively.
